summary: Confirmed that current admission accounting already prevents full-attention evictability from masking zero Mamba-slot capacity, but reproduced the remaining late prefill allocation exception escaping Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw. Added typed KV allocation misses, failed-call request-slot cleanup, chunk bookkeeping rollback, and request requeue/backpressure, with focused regression and boundary coverage.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before evidence: the injected KV allocation miss escaped the actual prefill scheduling method instead of returning the request to waiting_queue. Raw output: reports/j-c5ca6fd09709/failing_before_requeue.log

34 tests and 12 subtests passed, covering scheduler requeue, new versus pre-existing request-slot ownership, the issue-shaped exhausted-Mamba admission case, Mamba-evictable recovery, and ChunkCache boundary behavior. Raw output: reports/j-c5ca6fd09709/passing_after.log
Detected one AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and ROCm 7.2.26015. Raw output: reports/j-c5ca6fd09709/gpu_environment.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: Only device inventory was queried. The changed behavior is CPU scheduler/control flow and the deterministic regressions run on CPU; no GPU kernel result is claimed.

remaining_limitations: The exact Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP4 sustained-traffic reproduction was not run because the job provides one AMD gfx950 GPU rather than eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs and does not provide Kimi-K3 weights.
The tests validate allocation failure propagation, ownership cleanup, queue recovery, and admission boundaries; they do not validate Kimi-K3 semantic accuracy or distributed behavior.
The tiny Llama serving fixture was not used because it cannot exercise the hybrid Mamba allocator or qualify the reported architecture.
